channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: What Investors Want to Know About Trump and the Midterm Elections
item.description: Looking at historical returns offers some clues.
item.dc:creator: Nathan R Dean

item.title: Big Take: Benjamin Netanyahu’s Referendum Has Finally Arrived
item.description: For the first time since the October 7 attacks, Israelis are headed to the polls. The race is seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is neck-and-neck with opponent Gadi Eisenkot in the latest polls. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks Fall as Oil Rally Keeps a Lid on Treasuries
item.description: A resurgence in oil prices dragged down stocks and bonds, stoking concerns about inflation just days ahead of the next Fed decision. Brent crude topped $116 as a flare-up in Middle East violence threatened global supply. The S&P 500 saw back-to-back losses, even as selling pressure on tech firms abated. Yields rose after the market’s best day in more than a year. Joe Weisenthal, Bloomberg ‘Odd Lots’ Podcast Co-Host, joins to wrap up the week in markets ahead of the next Fed decision and more tech earnings. Jayati Bharadwaj, Head of FX Strategy at TD Securities, weighs in on a rush to safe haven trades. Plus, Bloomberg News AI Infrastructure Reporter Dina Bass joins to discuss her reporting on Blackstone's bet on chips driving a debt boom. Finally, Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry on internet security in light of new PHP vulnerabilities across the web. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Big Names Stir Michigan Senate Race
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Joe Mathieu discusses the latest from the White House. On today's show, Redwave Communications Owner David Kochel, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino, Friday Reporter Public Affairs Founder Lisa Camooso Miller and The States Project Co-Founder Daniel Squadron. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump 'Obsessed' With Undermining States' Independence, Says Daniel Squadron
item.description: Daniel Squadron, co-founder of The States Project and former New York state senator, said that state houses will serve a key role in the legitimacy of elections and that President Trump is 'obsessed with undermining the independence of states' as local governments administer elections. Squadron said that local elections are where cynicism about politics 'melts away' because of closeness of candidates to their constituents. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Has 'Work to Do' To Excite Iowa Voters, Says David Kochel
item.description: Iowa GOP strategist David Kochel said he thinks its good for Iowa's Republican candidates that Trump is campaigning in the state and that the president is 'going to the right places where we really need Republican enthusiasm to kick in here.' Kochel said that Republican Senate Candidate Ashley Hinson is the star of the 2026 midterm field but will still need to 'defy gravity' to win the election. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Khanna Says Zuckerberg Deal Shows Ultra-Rich Will Pay Wealth Tax
item.description: Progressive Democrat Ro Khanna lashed out at opponents of California’s proposed wealth tax after Meta Platforms Inc. revealed stunning details of how Chief Executive Officer Mark Zuckerberg negotiated a deal to fund his potential payment of the levy and stay in the state if the measure passes.
item.dc:creator: Josh Sisco

item.title: Trump Changes Some Canada Tariffs in Bid to Aid Maine Senator
item.description: The Trump administration is expanding tariff exemptions to more Canadian products, a move that may help boost Republican Senator Susan Collins’ reelection campaign in Maine.
item.dc:creator: Steven T. Dennis, Josh Wingrove and Greg Ryan

item.title: Macron Pledges to Overhaul University Admissions, AFP Says
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said he would overhaul the country’s university admissions platform during his first meeting with representatives of high school students who have been protesting for weeks, Agence France-Presse reported.
item.dc:creator: Frank Connelly

item.title: Magyar Praises Hungary-EU Ties on Day of Anti-Soviet Uprising
item.description: Prime Minister Peter Magyar used a commemoration of Hungary’s 1956 anti-Soviet uprising to reaffirm his country’s place in Europe, following years of pro-Moscow policies under his predecessor Viktor Orban.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Escritt

item.title: Trump Steps Up Support for Ramaswamy Ad Despite GOP Blowback
item.description: President Donald Trump stepped up his support for a controversial ad featuring the estranged mother of Ohio’s Democratic candidate for governor, Amy Acton, despite intensifying Republican opposition to the campaign spot.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: Kalshi CEO on Midterms, Regulation and Inflation Futures
item.description: Kalshi co-founder and CEO Tarek Mansour discusses the growing role of prediction markets in elections and the regulatory challenges facing the industry. Speaking with Tyler Kendall on "Bloomberg Tech," Mansour also comments on the company's proposed perpetual oil futures contract. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Netanyahu Has Isolated Israel
item.description: Broad backlash has left Israeli voters with a stark choice in this month’s election: Elect a government committed to regaining international confidence or further alienate the country’s traditional allies with Netanyahu and his far-right coalition, says Bloomberg Opinion columnist Ronald Brownstein. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ex-FBI Officials Charged Over Testimony on Hunter Biden Probe
item.description: Two former senior FBI officials were charged with making false statements to lawmakers about their involvement in investigations concerning Hunter Biden.
item.dc:creator: Myles Miller

item.title: Putin’s Temporary Control of Metro Unit Reaps Funds for War Push
item.description: The local unit of German grocer Metro said it committed 1 billion rubles ($12.4 million) to Russia’s war effort a month after Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered it be put into temporary administration.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Lovell Sees Earnings Growth Beyond AI
item.description: Nadia Lovell, UBS Global Wealth Management’s head of global equity strategy, said markets may remain volatile over the coming weeks amid earnings, next week’s Federal Reserve meeting, midterm-election uncertainty and the Middle East conflict’s impact on energy and oil prices. Despite risks around financing the AI buildout, she said economic growth and demand remain strong, with much of the investment led by high-quality hyperscalers. Lovell said investors should not abandon the AI trade, but should become more selective. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump, UK’s Burnham Set for Call as Tensions Rise Over Ukraine, Iran Policy
item.description: President Donald Trump spoke with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday as tensions build between the two governments over Russia’s war in Ukraine and the possibility of renewed US escalation against Iran.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain, Josh Wingrove and Alex Wickham

item.title: US Says Russia, Ukraine to Let Civilians Leave War-Torn Area
item.description: The White House said Friday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to allow for aid in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky and prepare an evacuation route for civilians, even as Kyiv complained that crucial Starlink service had yet to be restored.
item.dc:creator: Josh Wingrove and Piotr Skolimowski

item.title: EU Working on More China Curbs as Trade Deficit Heads for Record
item.description: The European Union is advancing plans to protect more sectors from surging Chinese imports, which the bloc’s trade chief warned may create a record deficit this year.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Valero and Olivia Fletcher

item.title: France Plans Military Presence to Contain Weekend Protests
item.description: French authorities are bracing for a new round of protests Saturday, rolling out the military to back up police in a bid to prevent a repeat of last weekend’s riots and reassure markets unnerved by the violence.
item.dc:creator: Benoit Berthelot
